## Adalysis Home page Redesign Concepts
- **Figma:** https://www.figma.com/design/VMrnmhXXIELsvUVBN16TSW/Adalysis---Home-page-concepts?node-id=1-4&t=auQE1GKyBCFUUaRd-1
- **Engagement:** Concept / test task
- **Deliverables:** Figma designs, Home concepts
- **Pages designed:** Home page, Landing page
- **Industry:** software / SaaS
- **Proof level:** Concept
- **Context:** All 5 concepts were built on the same content and the same product truth. What changed each time was how much of the page carried the argument and how much of it carried the interface. That was the point: give the client a few genuinely different layouts to react to instead of 5 variations of one idea. Keeping the spine fixed was deliberate. It meant the client was comparing visual language and layout logic each time instead of comparing content, so feedback came back about direction rather than wording. What changed between them was one decision: how early and how literally the product interface appears, and whether the page's rhythm is carried by the brand or by the software.
- **Design notes:** ⚡️ Adalysis Home page Redesign Concepts — design direction concepts for client exploration and brand perception refinement Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Adalysis-Home-Page-Redesignhttps://adalysis.com/
- **Bid line:** ⚡️ Adalysis - SaaS PPC Copilot tool where I designed multiple home page concepts as part of a brand redesign Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/VMrnmhXXIELsvUVBN16TSW/Adalysis---Home-page-concepts?m=auto&t=1rSMkJxQ3KCkVN2l-6 https://adalysis.com/

## B12 Coffee Webshop
- **Live:** https://b12.coffee/
- **Figma:** https://www.figma.com/design/5Fn9bNltWgSM13XPpjRnY3/B12-Coffee-Webshop?node-id=0-1&t=ZlCOXUWfeCQjAYhb-1
- **Engagement:** Design + build
- **Deliverables:** Figma designs, Live website, Brand identity
- **Pages designed:** Full site, Home page, PDP, Catalog / PLP
- **Stack:** Figma, For Shopify
- **Features:** E-commerce, For Shopify
- **Industry:** food, e-commerce, lifestyle
- **Proof level:** Live
- **Story:** Specialty coffee roastery in Düsseldorf selling single-origin coffee, equipment and ceramics, running barista and latte art courses and supplying cafés and offices as a wholesale partner. I designed the brand identity and the whole site, then built it on Shopify. The brand work set the b12 wordmark and the Specialty Coffee Roastery emblem, the forest green and cream palette and the Outfit type system, and a UI component library the rest of the site is assembled from. The shop covers the catalogue with filters, product pages for coffee and for merchandise, quick view, cart and search. The coffee school area carries the course range and a single course page, where enrolment runs through a course request that captures the course, the preferred date and the group size, with private event and gift flows as their own modals. The B2B area presents custom roasts, barista training, verified origin reports and equipment advice, with a partnership application and wholesale pricing behind a separate sign-up. Venue and catering, membership, sustainability and the legal pages complete the site, all designed at 1920, 1440, 744 and 360.
- **Context:** Coffee roastery with three audiences on one site: retail customers buying beans and ceramics, people booking barista and latte art courses, and cafés and offices applying for wholesale terms. The structure had to let each of the three find their own path without crowding the others.
- **Design notes:** Brand identity and full site design for b12, a specialty coffee roastery in Düsseldorf. Logotype and emblem, forest green and cream palette, Outfit type system and a UI component library, then the shop, coffee school with course enrolment, B2B wholesale, venue and catering, membership and sustainability areas across four breakpoints.
- **Dev notes:** Shopify development of the b12 storefront from the Figma designs: catalogue and filtering, product pages for coffee and merchandise, quick view, cart and search, plus the course request, private event, gift and B2B partnership application forms.
- **Showcase frames:** Upwork case boards (💼 - Upwork case page in the B12 file): Thumbnail https://www.figma.com/design/5Fn9bNltWgSM13XPpjRnY3/B12-Coffee-Webshop?node-id=7062-28311 | Course enrolment components https://www.figma.com/design/5Fn9bNltWgSM13XPpjRnY3/B12-Coffee-Webshop?node-id=7063-29465

## Beauty Label
- **Live:** https://beautylabel.us/
- **Engagement:** Design only
- **Deliverables:** Figma designs, Live website
- **Pages designed:** Full site, Home page, Catalog / PLP
- **Stack:** Figma
- **Features:** Booking, E-commerce
- **Industry:** lifestyle, e-commerce
- **Proof level:** Live
- **Story:** Beauty Label is a Brooklyn hair salon led by Mariana Sidey that calls itself a collective of artists and specialises in luxury blonde colour, extensions and general hair services. The site has to carry two jobs at once, filling the chair and moving retail product, so I designed the booking path as the spine and let the shop sit alongside it instead of competing with it. Appointment booking repeats down the page with a free 30-minute consultation as the low-commitment entry for first-time clients, and the salon retail shelf presents professional lines from Kérastase, Aveda, Moroccanoil and Oribe across new arrivals, tools, shampoo and conditioner, treatments and oils. Stylist profiles, partner brands and testimonials carry the credibility a colour specialist is judged on.
- **Context:** A salon that sells appointments and retail product from the same page, where the booking path had to stay dominant while the shop still functioned. Luxury blonde colour is a trust purchase, so stylist profiles, partner brands and reviews carry as much weight as the services list.
- **Design notes:** Website design for Beauty Label, a luxury blonde and hair extension salon in Brooklyn. Booking-led structure with a free consultation entry point, a salon retail shelf for professional haircare brands, stylist profiles and testimonials. Live: https://beautylabel.us/

## EX-PACK
- **Live:** https://expack.de/
- **Engagement:** Design only
- **Deliverables:** Figma designs, Live website
- **Pages designed:** Full site, Home page
- **Stack:** Figma
- **Industry:** industrial, professional services
- **Proof level:** Live
- **Story:** EX-PACK (Expeditions- und Verpackungsgesellschaft mbH) is an industrial logistics provider in Emmerich am Rhein, founded in 1988, handling fulfilment, warehousing, export packaging and transport for manufacturers shipping by air, sea, road and intermodal routes. The business sells services and not products, so the whole site has to earn a consultation request instead of a checkout. I designed the site around that single conversion: four service teasers off the hero, the eight industries they serve each routed to their own contact, a four-step explanation of how an order actually runs and an FAQ covering lead times, oversize freight, customs, insurance and damage, with the credibility figures of 35+ years, 40+ countries, 6,000 m² of warehouse and 1,000+ completed projects carried through the page. German-language site.
- **Context:** Services business with no shop and no catalogue, so every section has to move the visitor toward a Beratung anfordern consultation request and the non-binding quote that follows it. Eight industry segments needed their own entry point without turning the homepage into a directory. The live build appears to run on WordPress with Elementor, though that was not confirmed.

- **Pages designed:** Home page
- **Features:** For Shopify
- **Industry:** e-commerce, entertainment, food
- **Proof level:** Concept
- **Context:** Concept 01 = Modern Luxury This concept focuses on the product and conversion. I restructured the information hierarchy, removed repetitive messaging, unified the UI components, and created a cleaner layout so visitors could quickly understand the value of the Mystery Bourbon Box and move naturally toward the primary CTA. Visually, the direction creates a contemporary, high-end ecommerce experience with the product at its center. Concept 02 = The Curator’s Journal This concept shifts the emphasis toward brand storytelling. I reorganized the content flow so visitors first discover Whiskey Library’s philosophy and expertise before being introduced to the product. Editorial layouts, large-scale photography, and a curated archive of previous discoveries replace more conventional product sections. The direction is intended to build trust and position Whiskey Library as an exclusive whiskey club rather than a traditional ecommerce store.
- **Bid line:** Whiskey library wanted to relaunch their brand identity and how they sell the whiskey subscription on their website so we came up with 2 alternative home page concepts to explore how we could integrate new user journeys through elevated style: https://www.figma.com/design/D0evPXk6hygKzwvRYJqLnk/Whiskey-Library?node-id=2025-302&t=EjSEvYSQd1qDmxYg-1
